_doc: Ask on phone / Ask on computer: one mechanism, both ways. A device asks its peer to turn on a feature only the peer can turn on with desklink.settings.request {set: {<key>: true}}, <key> from the peer's table below (toPhone: the desk asks the phone; toDesk: the phone asks the desk). The peer NEVER turns anything on from the packet: it shows a prompt (a notification with Allow and Not now, and a banner in its app) and only the person's Allow there turns the feature on. toDesk keys are never settable keys (wire_values.json settings.settable keep their direct meaning). The answerer's state rides its desklink.settings report (the phone now sends one too): features (every key of its table -> on), declined (the keys the person just answered Not now: only in the report sent for that answer), prompts ('on', or 'off' when its notifications cannot show the prompt: the asker then says to open DeskLink there, where the banner waits). The asker: waiting from its ask until an answer or waitSeconds; declined; timedOut; undelivered (the ask could not be sent, retried once when the link is ready); blocked (prompts off). A feature reported on ends the ask in any state (an answer after the timeout still counts). One pending ask per key per device; an ask nobody pressed for (automatic) at most every reaskSeconds; the answerer replaces, never stacks, a prompt and drops a repeat within dedupeSeconds. Identical copies: protocol/testdata/desklink_v9/, DeskLink/testdata/, desklink-mobile/src/test/resources/shared/.

toPhone.photos: get your new photos and screenshots

words.blocked: Notifications are off on {device}: open DeskLink there to allow
